issues.legal_issue: A recorded occupant who is distinct from a tenant of sir and is in actual possession or enjoyment of the land takes adhivasi status in preference to that tenant.
material_facts: The dispute concerned land held by the landholder as sir and a claim to recover possession from a tenant of sir.
The court considered how the statutory scheme treated a tenant of sir when another person was recorded as occupant of the land and was in actual possession or enjoyment.
The court interpreted the provisions in light of the legislation’s object of removing intermediaries and establishing a direct relationship between the State and the tiller of the soil.
issues.conclusion: A distinct person recorded as occupant in the relevant land records, and actually possessing or enjoying the land, obtains adhivasi status in preference to a tenant of sir who is not in possession; the tenant’s claim under the tenant category does not displace that occupant’s priority.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 20(a)(i) and 20(a)(ii) confer adhivasi status on qualifying tenants of sir and sub-tenants, subject to the exception in section 20(b)(i), which gives priority to a qualifying recorded occupant. Section 21(1)(h) may deem an occupant within section 20(b)(i) an asami if its conditions are met. The expression “occupant” means a person holding the land in possession or actual enjoyment, as explained in Amba Prasad v. Abdul Noor Khan and affirmed in Nath Singh v. Board of Revenue. The interpretation is consistent with Kumari Radha Kishori v. Joint Director of Consolidation and the Act’s purpose of removing intermediaries; where statutory language permits competing interpretations, the interpretation advancing that purpose is preferred.

rule.if: land_possession_recovery_proceeding and sir_tenant_claims_adhivasi and distinct_person_recorded_as_occupant and distinct_person_in_actual_possession

predicates.land_possession_recovery_proceeding: A proceeding concerns recovery of possession of land under a land-tenure system.
predicates.sir_tenant_claims_adhivasi: A person who held the land as a tenant of sir claims adhivasi status.
predicates.distinct_person_recorded_as_occupant: The relevant land record identifies someone other than the tenant as the occupant of the land.
predicates.distinct_person_in_actual_possession: The person identified as occupant was in actual possession or enjoyment of the land.
predicates.distinct_recorded_occupant_has_adhivasi_: The distinct recorded occupant obtains adhivasi status in preference to the tenant of sir.

issues.definition: When a possession-recovery proceeding involves a tenant of sir claiming adhivasi status and a distinct recorded occupant who was actually possessing the land, the distinct recorded occupant has priority to adhivasi status.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant of sir who is not displaced by a distinct recorded occupant becomes an adhivasi under the tenant category and is not deemed an asami merely because the landholder is disabled.
material_facts: The landholder had held the disputed land as sir and had become its bhumidhar.
The defendants were tenants of sir and were recorded as tenants of sir in the relevant land records.
No one else was shown as the occupant of the disputed land in those records.
The landholder was a disabled person, and sought possession on the theory that the defendants were asamis.
The lower courts dismissed the possession suits, and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeals.
issues.conclusion: Because no distinct occupant was shown, the defendants became adhivasis under section 20(a)(i); section 21(1)(h) did not apply to make them asamis, and the suits for possession were rightly dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 20(a)(i) and 20(b)(i), read together, give adhivasi status to a tenant of sir when no distinct person is recorded as occupant, while section 21(1)(h)’s occupant limb applies to an occupant contemplated by section 20(b)(i), not to the tenant who obtains status under section 20(a)(i). The interpretation follows the statutory structure and the Act’s purpose of removing intermediaries. Amba Prasad v. Abdul Noor Khan, Nath Singh v. Board of Revenue, and Kumari Radha Kishori v. Joint Director of Consolidation support the meaning and priority of an occupant in actual possession or enjoyment.

predicates.land_possession_recovery_proceeding: A proceeding concerns recovery of possession of land under a land-tenure system.
predicates.sir_tenant_recorded_as_tenant: The person from whom possession is sought held the land as a tenant of sir and was recorded as such.
predicates.no_distinct_recorded_occupant: No person other than the tenant was shown as occupant of the land in the relevant land records.
predicates.tenant_becomes_adhivasi_not_asami: The tenant obtains adhivasi status and is not deemed an asami on the basis of the occupant category.

issues.definition: In a possession-recovery proceeding, a recorded tenant of sir becomes an adhivasi and not an asami when no distinct person is recorded as occupant.
